rows.name: server.prepareTriage
rows.reason: it starts an in-app triage of the T3 Code install itself: the server writes the session files `t3 triage` writes (its own logs, config and version under T3 home) and clones the T3 Code source from github.com/pingdotgg/t3code into its cache, then hands the phone a prompt for a scratch thread. t3-serve is not that server (it has no T3 home, logs or release to diagnose) and rca-exec has nothing of it to read; the feature would be a network clone of a third party's repository with no state of ours to triage, so there is nothing to build and prove on the executor. The phone's own fallback is the `npx t3 triage` command it offers to copy. Proposed default awaiting owner confirmation.

rows.name: subscribeResourceTelemetry
rows.reason: the stream is a process monitor of the T3 install itself: samples of the T3 server, its provider and terminal roots and the Electron processes (categories `server`, `provider-root`, `electron-main`, ...) taken by a protocol-3 resource-monitor sidecar, plus update state and host power. t3-serve has no such process tree and rca-exec has no process-sampling action; the one honest part, the executor host's CPU and memory, would ship with an empty process list that the phone's resource view would present as a healthy idle server. Proposed default awaiting owner confirmation.
